column3: The Hebrew says the article “shall be brought into water”; BSB specifies that it “must be rinsed with water.”
The Hebrew repeats food “which is eaten” and drink “which is drunk”; BSB omits these descriptions and explicitly supplies “from that pot” for the water.
The Hebrew repeats plural “they are unclean” and “they shall be unclean for you”; BSB uses singular “it” for the oven or pot.
The Hebrew does not explicitly say the carcass being touched is “in it”; BSB adds that location.
The Hebrew specifies seed “which shall be sown”; BSB gives only “seed for sowing.”
The Hebrew names creatures that “multiply feet” as a separate group after those walking on four; BSB combines these as “four or more feet.”
The Hebrew uses the detestable word first, then repeats the becoming-unclean word; BSB uses “defile,” “unclean,” and “defiled.”
The Hebrew describes the animals with passive “is eaten” and “shall not be eaten”; BSB expresses permission with “may be eaten” and “may not.”
